newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-REFEREE DEFENDS DECISION TO CALL OFF LIVERPOOL DERBY.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-REFEREE DEFENDS DECISION TO CALL OFF LIVERPOOL DERBY.

text.p: The referee who postponed the Merseyside derby between Liverpool and Everton less than an hour before kick-off on Sunday has defended his decision on safety grounds.
Roger Dilkes inspected the playing surface at Liverpool's Anfield ground at 1305 GMT and decided torrential overnight rain followed by more downpours on Sunday had made the pitch unplayable.
The match had been due to start at 1400 GMT in front of a sell-out crowd of 41,300. A further 6,000 fans were poised to watch the big clash on a giant television screen at Everton.

"I have a lot of sympathy for the fans. Both clubs are big clubs and their fans come from all around the country," Dilkes said. "But I couldn't let that influence my decision. I had to look at the players' safety alone.
"Despite the strenuous efforts of the groundstaff the weather was always going to beat them. As fast as they were taking the water off it was coming down even faster."
No new date has yet been set for the match.
